claims.text: In artifact `e4fc47f3922256c6c42246975f40ffc6894f31d042bf76d1691cdcac46288d54`, every recorded non-boundary degree \(d\in\{7,\ldots,24\}\) has fields `U:null` and `V:null`; only `operationLog` and Boolean replay-check fields are retained. [artifact d87baeaea5da98a1f5f739cd580d3919cb2ecc7a1c0e295789de0e8e05ef0b6f@L1-L28]

At the boundary \(d=6\), the artifact records \(M_6=D_6=0_{0\times1}\), \(U_6=I_0=0_{0\times0}\), and \(V_6=[1]\), so \(U_6M_6V_6=D_6\) and \(\det(U_6)=\det(V_6)=1\). [artifact d87baeaea5da98a1f5f739cd580d3919cb2ecc7a1c0e295789de0e8e05ef0b6f@L1-L28]

Explicit witness persistence requires stored integer arrays \(U_d\in\mathbb Z^{m_d\times m_d}\), \(V_d\in\mathbb Z^{n_d\times n_d}\) for each \(M_d\in\mathbb Z^{m_d\times n_d}\), permitting direct evaluation of \(U_dM_dV_d=D_d\). Since JSON `null` is not an integer matrix, this requirement fails for every recorded \(d\ge7\).
An operation log, even accompanied by a successful replay assertion, is distinct from persisted matrices \(U_d,V_d\); it therefore cannot satisfy the stated literal persistence requirement.
